questions.q: Why does Day call your twenties a good time to fail?
a: It is a time to discover who you are before adult life
It is when employers expect the most mistakes
It is the only period when failure is forgiven
It is when your brain stops developing
questions.why: Lesson one says the twenties are for discovering what you want before adult responsibilities pile up.

questions.q: What did Day learn from her divorce?
a: She had been trying to complete herself through partners
She needed a partner who shared her chores
She had married too young to know herself
She should have focused only on her career
questions.why: Lesson two says reflecting on her relationships showed her a pattern of using other people to feel whole.

questions.q: What does Day say about staying open after a painful heartbreak?
a: It is important not to close yourself off
It is safer to avoid dating for years
It is best to jump into a new relationship
It is natural to stop trusting everyone
questions.why: The summary says one of her most important lessons was to remain open even after being hurt.

questions.q: What did Day discover about famous and wealthy people?
a: Success did not make them immune to unhappiness
They were happier than ordinary people
They rarely experienced failure again
They valued money more than relationships
questions.why: Lesson three says the actors she interviewed showed that money and fame do not guarantee happiness.

questions.q: What did Robert Pattinson say fame cost him?
a: His privacy and sense of control over his life
His closest friendships and family ties
His interest in acting and music
His health and physical fitness
questions.why: Lesson three says Pattinson struggled with isolation and a lack of personal control after becoming famous.
